findings.evidence: _GraphifyIndexLoader builds the shared index with skill_memory=_orchestrator.skill_memory (legacy, install-wide). _build_user_context creates a per-user SkillMemory (server.py ~line 469) but _MemoryScopedGraphifyView copies every non-memory record of the shared index unchanged, so 'skill:<tool>:<task_type>:<domain>' records learned by the legacy/primary user reach every signed-in user's relevant_subset hint, and a user's own learned skills never appear. AC5 keeps this on purpose; it already existed and is outside the memory-pointer scope of this milestone.
findings.suggested_fix: Owner decides whether skill: records should be per-user; if so, rebuild the skill scope from the context's own SkillMemory, the same way the memory scope is rebuilt.
findings.title: Non-memory skill: records in every user's view still come from the install-wide legacy SkillMemory, not the user's own per-user SkillMemory
